_about: Combat constants for the simulation (scripts/sim/combat_rules.gd reads this; scripts/sim/combat.gd, combat_resolver.gd and the World use it). ALL PROPOSED by Track C, 2026-10-09, for the first fight: Alex decided the model (a cone per weapon on a hardpoint, hits random-ish, machine-gun odds better near the cone's centre, the same cone in height, the host resolves and sends the result; and that a dead plane either explodes mid air or loses control and crashes eventually) but none of these numbers. Every tunable is a value record: {value, _proposed, _reason} until a decision replaces _proposed with a decision id. The per-weapon numbers (cones, range, odds, damage, roll rate) are in data/units/<id>.json under 'weapons'.

tick_seconds._reason: the lead's brief: combat walks the turn at a fixed tick. 0.25 s is 20 ticks per 5 s turn: finer than the shortest motion step (a 5-step fighter's step is 1 s), so a pass through a cone is seen, and cheap enough that a turn resolves in milliseconds. The turn is cut into round(turn_seconds / tick_seconds) equal ticks, so the last tick always ends exactly on the turn

target_rule._reason: a default so a weapon with several enemies in its cone still rolls at one of them: the one with the best odds (ties: nearer, then the unit added first). NOT target priority, which Alex will design; when he does, this record names the new rule

odds_factors._reason: the named factors that multiply a weapon's base_hit_chance, in this order. 'centre' (better odds nearer the cone's centre, per weapon falloff) and 'range' (1 inside the effective range, falling smoothly to 0 slightly over it) are Alex's (2026-10-09). Crossing speed, damage and others come later by adding a name here and a function in combat.gd; none is built

range_overshoot._reason: Alex 2026-10-09: a gun fires 'slightly over effective range'. Past a weapon's effective_range_m the 'range' factor falls along a smoothstep (flat at the effective range, flat again at the end) to 0 at effective range x (1 + this). 0.2 is a fifth: 400 m becomes 480, 450 becomes 540, 600 becomes 720 -- far enough that a stand-off just outside the range still gets shot at (a fighter 420 m behind the bomber is 409.5 m from its tail turret, inside the fringe at about 96 percent of full odds) and short enough that 'slightly' stays true; the range 0.15 to 0.25 would all do. One number for every weapon; per weapon later if a gun needs its own

max_pitch_deg._reason: while a plane changes altitude band its guns tilt with the climb or dive: the cone's axis pitches by the path's angle, atan(vertical speed / speed), at most this much either way. Bands are 280 to 600 m apart and a step is 1 to 1.7 s, so the raw angle is always 60 to 80 degrees; this caps it at about the 37 degree dive drawn on the engagement-cones sheet. 0 turns the tilt off (the cone stays level in a climb or dive)

explode_chance._reason: Alex 2026-10-09: a dead plane either explodes mid air or loses control and crashes eventually. The lead's proposed split: this chance it explodes at once, otherwise it falls out of control. One seeded roll per kill (its own stream, combat.gd fate_seed). Per-weapon or overkill factors come later, not now

fall_turn_rate_dps._reason: an out-of-control plane turns at this fixed rate, to the left or the right as the same roll says: a spiral. About a light fighter's sustained turn at slow speed (data/units: 30 deg/s at 45 m/s), so at cruise it spirals on a circle of about 190 m radius

fall_speed_gain_mps2._reason: it holds speed and gains this much per second as it falls (gravity beats drag), up to the unit type's dive_speed_max_mps. 4 m/s^2 is the light fighter's own acceleration

fall_descent_mps._reason: metres of height lost per second while out of control. From the high band (1000 m) that is 20 s, 4 turns; from medium (400 m) 8 s, 1.6 turns; from low (120 m) 2.4 s. Slow enough that the fall is watched over a turn or two, fast enough that it is a fall and not a glide. The sim has no terrain: the ground is 0 m
